title: Exploitation Analyst (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799, 2629), DC I
raw_text:
3. MOS 1713, Exploitation Analyst (MGySgt to Pvt) NMOS (1721, 1799, 2629),
DC I

    a. Summary. This NMOS requires advanced analytical training.
Exploitation Analysts are the primary technical planners for offensive
cyberspace operations. The Exploitation Analyst must be an expert with
adversary systems, networks, technologies, tools, techniques, and procedures.
The duties for MOS 1713 encompass generating intelligence, converting
intelligence to operational planning, developing significant target
awareness, and balancing levels of risk against operational goals. Duties
increase with experience to encompass the management of target packages and
developing new techniques and procedures for offensive cyber operations.

    b. Prerequisites. Must be currently assigned to one of the following
PMOSs 1721, 1799, or 2629.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete training and certification standards as determined by
the national security agency or United States Cyber Command.

        (2) MOS 1713 assigned upon approval of the Director, Information
Maneuver Division.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to NAVMC
3500.124A, Information Maneuver Training and Readiness Manual.

    e.      Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
None.

       f.   Related Military Skill

            (1) Offensive Cyberspace Warfare Officer, 1710.

            (2) Interactive On-Net Operator, 1712.

            (3) Cyberspace Warfare Operator, 1721.

            (4) Cyberspace Warfare Chief, 1799.
common_text: The Information Maneuver Occupational Field integrates information capability areas and the military occupational specialties (MOS) of cyberspace, space, electromagnetic warfare, civil affairs, and psychological operations into a single OCCFLD. Marines from these disciplines utilize their exquisite talents, knowledge, skills, and abilities to generate, preserve, and apply informational power against a relevant actor in order to increase or protect competitive advantage or combat power potential within all domains of the operating environment. Duty assignments include Marine Corps Forces Cyberspace Command, Marine Corps Forces Space Command, Marine Corps Information Command, Marine Cryptologic Support Battalion, Marine Corps Information Operations Center, MEF information groups, HQMC, MARFORs, joint organizations, and staff sections at all levels of the MAGTF.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
